stage: Implementation validation before the subsequent clean-code review
issue: A tool batch or temporary compaction request can jump past the context capacity
behavior: The application supplies each DeepAgent node with the discovered context capacity and a complete-request token estimator.
A request over budget forces compaction even when the threshold policy is disarmed or there are no replaceable messages.
Compaction exports eligible tool bodies to node-scoped files when its scoring prompt does not fit, including bodies below the ordinary 5000-token limit.
System, user, active skill instructions and original archived messages are preserved. Existing file references are not exported recursively.
Oversized catalogs are scored in disjoint batches. Oversized summary sources are processed in lossless chunks and combined; lack of reduction stops the operation.
After compaction and steering delivery, the runtime checks the next request again and stops explicitly if protected input or insufficient reduction still prevents it from fitting.
New history rearms the threshold policy even if a previous compaction stayed above 80%. Root context invalidation also clears obsolete native skill checkpoints.

request_budget.estimator: Literal DS4 Qwen prompt plus structured-output instruction and schema
request_budget.unknown_capacity: No fabricated context limit; the budget is not installed

scope: The guard uses the discovered capacity and supplied estimator; it cannot make oversized protected system/user input reducible.

The live test starts with a synthetic imported oversized history. Unit tests also cover a sub-5000-token tool output crossing the remaining budget, disarmed policies, insufficient compaction, export failure, empty and already-external outputs, batched scoring and bounded summaries.
No inference kernels, server protocols or cache payload formats changed. Metal, SSD streaming and distributed inference were not retested.
